questions.q: Which scheduling algorithm may cause starvation for some processes?
questions.e: Shortest Job Next always picks the shortest job, so long jobs can wait forever (starvation).

questions.q: Which scheduling algorithm allows a process to run for a fixed time before switching to another process?
questions.e: Round Robin gives each process a fixed time slice in turn.

questions.q: What does RAID stand for in data storage?
questions.e: RAID stands for Redundant Array of Independent Disks.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a mutex in multithreading?
o: To ensure only one thread accesses a resource at a time
questions.e: A mutex is a lock. Only one thread can hold it, so only one thread uses the resource at a time.

questions.q: In operating systems, what is thrashing?
o: Frequent swapping of pages between memory and disk
questions.e: Thrashing happens when the system spends most of its time swapping pages in and out instead of running programs.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a semaphore in an OS?
questions.e: A semaphore is a counter that lets processes take turns using a shared resource (synchronisation).

questions.q: Which scheduling algorithm can lead to starvation?
questions.e: Shortest Job Next can starve long jobs.

questions.q: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
o: Threads do not use CPU, but processes do
Threads share the same memory space, processes do not
Processes share memory, threads do not
questions.e: Threads of one process share its memory. Separate processes have their own memory.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a paging mechanism in memory management?
o: Mapping virtual addresses to physical addresses
questions.e: Paging maps virtual addresses to physical addresses through a page table.

questions.q: Which algorithm is used for deadlock avoidance?
questions.e: The Banker's algorithm checks that granting a request keeps the system in a safe state, so it avoids deadlock.

questions.q: Which of the following scheduling algorithms is preemptive?
questions.e: Round Robin is preemptive: the running process is stopped when its time slice ends.

questions.q: Which operating system component is responsible for process scheduling?
questions.e: The kernel contains the scheduler that decides which process runs.

questions.q: What is the purpose of memory segmentation?
o: Increase memory efficiency by dividing memory into segments
Allow for fast random access memory (RAM) access
Allow programs to run without fragmentation
questions.e: Segmentation splits memory into logical parts such as code, data and stack.

questions.q: In virtual memory management, what is a page fault?
o: When a process exceeds its memory allocation
When a program finishes its execution
When a page is not in the physical memory but is referenced
When the system runs out of physical memory
questions.e: A page fault happens when a program refers to a page that is not in physical memory.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the command "apt-get" in Linux-based systems?
questions.e: apt-get installs software packages on Debian-based Linux.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the command "ls" in Unix-like operating systems?
o: List files and directories in a directory
questions.e: ls lists files and folders.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the "grep" command in Unix-like operating systems?
o: Find and manipulate text within files
Search for files in a directory
questions.e: grep finds lines of text that match a pattern.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the command "chmod" in Unix-like operating systems?
questions.e: chmod changes file permissions.

questions.q: What is the primary function of an operating system?
questions.e: The operating system manages the hardware resources.

questions.q: Which of the following is a part of the Central Processing Unit?
questions.e: The ALU is part of the CPU. The other options are peripherals.

questions.q: The instructions that tell a computer how to carry out the processing tasks are referred to as computer___________?
questions.e: Programs are the instructions that tell a computer what to do.

questions.q: An area of a computer that temporarily holds data waiting to be processed is___________?
questions.e: Memory holds data waiting to be processed.

questions.q: Operating System is like a ___?
questions.e: An operating system governs and shares out the computer's resources, a bit like a government.
